_note: RANKED METRO UNIVERSE for the rigging/machinery-moving lead engine. tier 1 = 48 live city hubs (in locations.json). tier 2 = next wave. tier 3 = expansion. status 'live' = city hub already built; 'queued' = to add in waves. 'industry' = the real industrial driver that makes each page genuinely local (uniqueness-engine input). Crane & heavy-haul city variants intentionally EXCLUDED per cluster analysis (unwinnable vs national incumbents). Review/approve before wiring to generators.

GE Aviation, machine tools & advanced manufacturing

_detailNote: PER-METRO SUBSTANCE, researched 2026-09-21. This is the matrix differentiation fix. A service x city page runs ~1,550 words and the only per-city input used to be the 4-word 'industry' string above (Omaha: 'rail & ag manufacturing'), which measured the four city matrices at 31-32% page-specific content against a 33% floor, with 86-88 of 113 pages under it. build-service-cities.js now reads these fields and each service frames them in its own words - see METRO_COPY there, and note that each service deliberately draws a DIFFERENT mix so the same facts do not produce the same sentences across four pages for one city. Every value is a verifiable public fact: named industrial districts and parks, the Class I railroads that actually serve the metro, real navigable freight water access, the dominant industrial building stock. An absent field means the research could not confirm it - 'port' is absent for inland metros by design; the 15 metros that had no 'stock' were filled 2026-10-19 from sourced research (CRE listings, NRHP/state historic records, port and economic-development pages), with single-listing figures such as clear heights deliberately left out. NEVER add an unverified fact here: it lands on four live pages per metro, and an unverifiable claim repeated across 88 metros is worse than a generic one. Metros with no entry keep their previous page output byte-for-byte.
_anchorsNote: WAVE 3 SECTOR ANCHORS, researched 2026-10-19 (raw per-batch output in data/wave3-research/). detail[key].anchors = { health, research, print, datacenter, energy: [named real institutions/facilities], buildings: one sentence, grade: {sector: strong|some|none} }. lib/waves.js sector-matches the 7 specialty services on these grades; a grade with an empty list never counts. Anchors are named on pages as what EXISTS in the metro, never as clients. Removed before merge because not operating as of 2026-10-19: Intel Ohio One, Google West Memphis, Digital Realty Charlotte, Meta El Paso, Meta Montgomery, AWS Ridgeland, Duane Arnold; Savannah research (Gulfstream/Hyundai are plants, not labs). Many newspaper print plants closed 2023-2026 and were deliberately left out - print is the thinnest sector. Tissue, newsprint and specialty-paper mills (Mobile, Baton Rouge, Savannah, Spokane, Hartford) and an unconfirmed LA mill were also dropped from print: a paper mill is not a press shop.
